The manipulation of time in the story is exceptionally well-balanced and serves the emotional weight of the narrative. In terms of "story time," the entire scene takes place over just a couple of minutes—the brief window between the delivery van flashing its lights on the opposite bank and Ilse preparing the ferry to cross. 

The author gently stretches this brief moment by weaving in sensory details (the click of the suitcase handle, the cold metal of the switchbox, the peeling shoe sole) and micro-flashbacks that compress years of shared family history and estrangement into single sentences (e.g., memories of Jonas refusing a hood in the rain, or the tense dynamic with Henning at the kitchen table). This slowing down of the present moment effectively mirrors the characters' hesitation, awkwardness, and unspoken emotional distance, while the impatient flashing of the delivery van's headlights anchors the scene in real-time, providing a subtle, rhythmic urgency that keeps the pacing from feeling stagnant.
